statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ front-month is near 29,645 (+0.27%) inside a 29,530.50-29,682.50 band roughly 0.51% wide that has now contained about eleven hours of trade; the overnight high has not been retested since it was made and rejected. Tail eases one point to 5 because the oil impulse is fading rather than building, with Brent about $96.10 against a $97.58 peak earlier this morning and WTI about $90.96, and because the index complex remains divergent, with ES near flat and YM about -0.5% against a bid NQ. Stress eases to 54 on the same oil retreat, but stays elevated on an unresolved Iranian restricted-zone announcement near the Strait of Hormuz, holiday-thinned depth with US cash equity and Treasury markets closed for Labor Day, and roughly 60% implied odds of a 25bp Fed hike on 15-16 September. Confidence holds at 85 on two current futures feeds, live European cash levels, current oil and yield readings and a verified calendar, tempered by one stale delayed feed and reduced holiday observation quality.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and Tail remains far below the block threshold in every hour of this outlook. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the shortened Labor Day futures halt, and secondarily at the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, rather than spread across the whole session. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a narrow overnight band as the oil spike fades, European cash slips and US markets stay shut for Labor Day
body:
The observation that changed this hour is oil. Brent peaked near $97.58 and WTI near $92.69 in the early European hours after the weekend US strikes on three Iranian tankers; both have since retreated, to roughly $96.10 and $90.96. A geopolitical premium that decays intraday is the opposite of the amplifier that matters for this strategy, so Tail eases a point to 5 and Stress eases to 54.

The NQ price path supports the same reading. The band from 29,530.50 to 29,682.50 has now contained about eleven hours of trade, roughly 0.51% wide. The high was made, rejected, and has not been retested; price has drifted from about 29,663.50 an hour ago to about 29,645 without either extending or breaking down. That is two-way containment, not the persistent directional efficiency that would justify a higher tail value.

Cross-asset alignment is absent in two directions at once. Within the US complex, NQ is up about 0.27% while S&P 500 futures are near flat and Dow futures are about 0.5% lower. Across regions, European cash is soft, with the STOXX 600 down 0.14% and the DAX down 0.32% against a marginally higher CAC 40. The NQ bid is narrow and identifiable: Asian memory and semiconductor names led a regional rally, with the KOSPI up 3.4% and the Nikkei up 1.9%. Narrow leadership against divergent broad indices reduces directional conviction; it does not create a one-way index path.

What keeps Stress elevated rather than low is structural, not price-based. US cash equity and Treasury markets are closed for Labor Day and CME equity index futures run a shortened session that halts near 17:00 UTC, so the European afternoon trades with no cash backstop and thinning depth. Iran has signalled a restricted maritime zone outside the Strait of Hormuz within days, an unresolved discontinuity through which roughly one fifth of global oil consumption passes, even though flows are currently running slightly above 9 million barrels a day under Navy escort. And the rate backdrop has turned hawkish: August payrolls of 162,000 against about 56,000 expected have lifted implied odds of a 25bp Fed hike on 15-16 September to roughly 60%, with the 10-year at 4.78% before the cash market closed and a 25bp ECB hike near fully priced for Thursday.

The danger window is left where the evidence puts it, at 15:00-17:00 UTC. That is the European cash close running into the futures halt, the thinnest expected depth of the day, and the point at which any unresolved Hormuz development would have to be priced rather than deferred to a US cash session that does not exist today. Conditional Tail reaches 8 there and 8 again at the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, both still deep inside the low band.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday session, mapping to EA_ON and green in every available hour, stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart to carry reopen-gap risk, eased back to 5 once that restart proved orderly, lifted to 7 when the overnight high extended, and eased to 6 in the most recent hour after that high was retraced. Stress moved through a 54 to 60 band, peaking at 60 into the Sunday close before settling in the mid-50s across the Asian session. Confidence stayed in a narrow 84 to 86 range throughout. Dominant mode was normal in every available hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the remainder of the European morning and a holiday afternoon traded against closed US cash equity and Treasury markets, a shortened futures session that halts near 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, and the Tuesday Asian session into the European open. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band in every hour: 5 for the current hour, 6 across the European morning and the holiday afternoon where thinned depth meets no US cash backstop, 8 in the flagged 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European close into the halt, 5 falling to 4 across the closed hours, 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart for reopen-gap risk, and 7 easing to 6 through the Tuesday Asian session. Stress runs 54 to 58 while the venue is open, steps down to 46 to 50 across the halt, and returns to 55 to 57 from the restart onward as the ECB decision, Thursday PPI and Friday CPI come into view. Confidence decays steadily from 85 to a floor of 70 at the far end, reflecting horizon rather than any expected change in conditions. Every hour maps to EA_ON and green, and dominant mode is normal throughout.
